SUMMARY:
The dominant build cost, and the method is now settled. 86 of 164 modules opened with a bare 'import Mathlib'; measured on Cohomology/SheafCompose.lean (49 lines), 16.6 s and about 7 GB with the umbrella versus 3.5 s and 1.97 GB with four precise imports. ORDERING RULE, learned the expensive way. Bottom-up is right for probe CORRECTNESS -- a module's minimal imports cannot be computed until everything beneath it is clean -- but wrong for NET PROGRESS whenever the module has a cone of import-less dependents above it. Narrowing StructureSheafModuleK/Presheaf.lean stripped the library from nine modules in the StructureSheafModuleK -> Genus -> Jacobian chain. Over wave 2, converting 8 modules forced 25 back onto the umbrella and the count went 39 back up to 64. Give a module's import-less dependents their own precise imports FIRST, top-down within the cone, then narrow the parent.

THE REAL WORK ITEM is the 54 modules that declare no Mathlib import at all and inherit the library transitively. They are invisible to the minimal-import probe because nothing in their own text says what they need, and every one that gets its own imports permanently removes a class of breakage. Elaborating all 54 in parallel with 'lake env lean' (read-only against .lake/build, safe alongside a running build) resolves the whole exposure in minutes; a full build finds only one victim per round because lake stops at the first failure in a chain. Of the 54, exactly 24 needed Mathlib -- the other 30 were loading 1.79 GB of oleans for nothing and are pure wins.
